<!-- Generated by pnpm reference:generate. Do not edit. -->

This page lists the public globals added by neo-js, not QuickJS built-ins or private host callbacks.

The host always installs `console`. `os` requires registration of `neojs-os` and allowlist admission of `neo:os`. `URL` requires admission of `neo:path`. Neither needs a permission flag. `env` requires `--allow-env` and admission of `neo:env`. `fs` requires `--allow-fs` and admission of `neo:fs`. See [host permissions and module access](/runtime/permissions/).

## console

The declaration file does not currently declare `console`. The host implements these synchronous methods and joins their string arguments with spaces before writing a line to stdout or stderr.

```ts
declare const console: {
  log(...args: string[]): void;
  error(...args: string[]): void;
};
```

## URL

The host installs a [file-only `URL` constructor](/guides/modules/path/#file-urls). The declaration file describes it as [`FileURLConstructor`](/api/modules/path/#fileurlconstructor) without redeclaring the DOM or WebWorker global.

## env

```ts
// Generated declarations for the selected compiled modules. Do not edit.
// Inputs: types/neo-js.core.d.ts, neojs-os/types/neo-os.d.ts, neojs-os-user/types/neo-os-user.d.ts, neojs-schedulers/types/neo-schedulers.d.ts, neojs-sqlite/types/neo-sqlite.d.ts
// Selection: core, os, os-user, schedulers, sqlite
// See types/README.md for the compose-types command.

/// <reference lib="esnext.disposable" />

// Core declarations for neojs-core. Optional modules owned by separate crates
// are added by composition; see types/README.md. This file deliberately omits
// `neo:os`, the scheduler generators, and `neo:sqlite`, because neojs-core
// does not compile or register them.

/** Available only with --allow-env. */
declare const env: {
  get(name: string): string | undefined;
  has(name: string): boolean;
};
```

## fs

```ts
/**
 * The `neo:fs` API. Available only with `--allow-fs` and when the runtime's
 * module allowlist admits `neo:fs`. Relative paths use the runtime's working
 * directory, not the host process's. `readFile`, `writeFile`, `writeText`,
 * `stat`, `lstat`, `readDir`, `mkdir`, and `remove` are asynchronous; their
 * `Sync` counterparts and every other operation block.
 *
 * This is not a sandbox: a script with this object has the host user's
 * filesystem authority. Reads and writes are bounded; see the `neo:fs`
 * declaration for the limits and the symlink and deletion rules.
 */
declare const fs: {
  readText(path: string): string;
  /**
   * Write text during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this throws
   * `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. Invalid arguments and
   * I/O errors reject the Promise. A started write can outlive a failed turn
   * and may truncate or complete the file after cancellation; an I/O failure
   * can leave partial data. There is no durability or concurrent-ordering
   * guarantee. The same outstanding-operation and worker limits as `readFile`
   * apply. See `neo:fs.writeText`.
   */
  writeText(path: string, data: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Same text validation and error precedence as `neo:fs.writeTextSync`. */
  writeTextSync(path: string, data: string): void;
  /**
   * Read bytes during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this throws
   * `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. At most four filesystem
   * operations are outstanding and two can run on workers. There is no caller
   * cancellation API; teardown cancels cooperatively and may wait for an OS
   * call.
   */
  readFile(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  readFileSync(path: string): Uint8Array;
  /**
   * Write bytes during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this throws
   * `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. Invalid arguments and
   * I/O errors reject the Promise. A started write can outlive a failed turn
   * and may truncate or complete the file after cancellation; an I/O failure
   * can leave partial data. There is no durability or concurrent-ordering
   * guarantee. The same outstanding-operation and worker limits as `readFile`
   * apply. See `neo:fs.writeFile`.
   */
  writeFile(
    path: string,
    data: Uint8Array,
    options?: import("neo:fs").WriteFileOptions,
  ): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Write bytes synchronously. An I/O failure can leave partial data. There
   * is no durability or concurrent-ordering guarantee. See
   * `neo:fs.writeFileSync`.
   */
  writeFileSync(
    path: string,
    data: Uint8Array,
    options?: import("neo:fs").WriteFileOptions,
  ): void;
  /**
   * Read metadata during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this throws
   * `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. It uses the same
   * outstanding-operation and worker limits as `readFile`. See
   * `neo:fs.stat` for the failure and result rules.
   */
  stat(path: string): Promise<import("neo:fs").FileInfo>;
  /** Same snapshot and error rules as `neo:fs.statSync`. */
  statSync(path: string): import("neo:fs").FileInfo;
  /**
   * Read metadata without following a final symlink during managed module
   * evaluation. Outside it, this throws `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN`
   * synchronously before I/O. See `neo:fs.lstat`.
   */
  lstat(path: string): Promise<import("neo:fs").FileInfo>;
  /** Same snapshot and error rules as `neo:fs.lstatSync`. */
  lstatSync(path: string): import("neo:fs").FileInfo;
  exists(path: string): boolean;
  /**
   * List a directory during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this throws
   * `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. It uses the same
   * outstanding-operation and worker limits as `readFile`. See `neo:fs.readDir`.
   */
  readDir(path: string): Promise<import("neo:fs").DirEntry[]>;
  /** Same sorted, bounded listing and error rules as `neo:fs.readDirSync`. */
  readDirSync(path: string): import("neo:fs").DirEntry[];
  /**
   * Create a directory during managed module evaluation. Outside it, this
   * throws `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O. It uses the same
   * outstanding-operation and worker limits as `readFile`. It follows
   * intermediate symlinks and provides no path containment. See
   * `neo:fs.mkdir` for the full symlink, failure, and race rules.
   */
  mkdir(path: string, options?: import("neo:fs").MkdirOptions): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Create a directory synchronously. It has the same final and intermediate
   * symlink behavior and no containment as `neo:fs.mkdirSync`.
   */
  mkdirSync(path: string, options?: import("neo:fs").MkdirOptions): void;
  /**
   * Remove a file, symlink, or directory during managed module evaluation.
   * Outside it, this throws `FS_ASYNC_OUTSIDE_TURN` synchronously before I/O.
   * It uses the same outstanding-operation, worker, and turn-budget limits as
   * `readFile`. An intermediate directory symlink is followed by the OS, so
   * deletion can land outside the apparent tree, and a component can change
   * between validation and use. See `neo:fs.remove` for the full symlink,
   * error, and race rules.
   */
  remove(path: string, options?: import("neo:fs").RemoveOptions): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Remove a file, symlink, or directory synchronously. It has the same entry,
   * intermediate-symlink, time-of-check/time-of-use, and no-rollback rules as
   * `neo:fs.removeSync`.
   */
  removeSync(path: string, options?: import("neo:fs").RemoveOptions): void;
  /** Same entry, replacement, and error semantics as `neo:fs.rename`. */
  rename: typeof import("neo:fs").rename;
  /** Same bounded, no-clobber copy as `neo:fs.copyFile`. */
  copyFile: typeof import("neo:fs").copyFile;
  FsError: typeof import("neo:fs").FsError;
  MAX_PATH_BYTES: number;
  MAX_READ_BYTES: number;
  MAX_WRITE_BYTES: number;
  MAX_LIST_ENTRIES: number;
  MAX_LIST_NAME_BYTES: number;
  MAX_LIST_TOTAL_BYTES: number;
};
```

## os

```ts
// Type fragment owned by neojs-os. The CLI composition includes it because the
// CLI links this crate. Declaring `neo:os` records compiled availability; it
// does not grant permission (none is needed) or admit the module through a
// runtime allowlist. types/neo-js.core.d.ts omits both this module and the
// `os` global.

/**
 * Host OS information. `platform` and `arch` identify the Rust compilation
 * target, not necessarily a separately detected host. Optional fields follow
 * the same platform-specific rules as the `neo:os` exports. This discloses
 * bounded, best-effort OS metadata without filesystem or registry permission;
 * it does not grant arbitrary filesystem or registry access or invoke a
 * subprocess. The object exists only when the host links `neojs-os`,
 * registers its extension, and admits `neo:os` in any explicit runtime
 * module allowlist. No permission flag is required. Global properties
 * remain writable; named module exports use the runtime's private snapshot.
 */
declare const os: {
  platform: string;
  arch: string;
  version: string | undefined;
  codename: string | undefined;
  variant: string | undefined;
};
```
